title: The Miracles and Healings of Jesus
subtitle: Thirty-five miracles and how they happened: who came to whom, what Jesus spoke to, when he touched, and whose faith is named
summary: "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and he went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with him" (Acts 10:38). This study looks closely at the ordinary details of each miracle: whether the sick came, were carried, or were sought out; whether Jesus spoke to the sickness or to the person; when he touched and when he only spoke; and whose faith the text names. The Patterns chart counts them. The last view follows the same works into the lives of his followers.

categories.title: The same event, told again
categories.note: Another Gospel's account of the same miracle.

categories.title: Foreshadowed
categories.note: An Old Testament promise or pattern the miracle answers to.

categories.title: Done again by his followers
categories.note: Where the apostles and the church did the same kind of work in his name.

facets.title: Who started it
facets.note: Whether Jesus went to them, or someone else made the first move.

values.title: Jesus went to them
values.note: No one asked. Jesus saw the need and acted first.

values.title: They came or cried out
values.note: The person in need came, called out, or reached for him.

values.title: Others brought them
values.note: Friends, family or neighbors carried or led them to Jesus.

values.title: Someone asked for them
values.note: A parent, a master, sisters or friends asked on their behalf.

facets.title: What he spoke to
facets.note: Jesus's words at the moment of the miracle. One event can have more than one.

values.title: The sickness, spirit or storm
values.note: He rebuked a fever, ordered a spirit out, or spoke to wind, sea or tree.

values.title: The person, declaring it done
values.note: Be clean. Be opened. Your faith has healed you. Your son will live.

values.title: The person, telling them to act
values.note: Get up. Stretch out your hand. Go and wash. Fill the jars.

values.title: The Father, in prayer or thanks
values.note: He gave thanks or prayed aloud before the miracle.

values.title: No healing words recorded
values.note: The text records no words to the sick person, the sickness or the Father.

facets.title: How it happened
facets.note: The physical side of the miracle. One event can have more than one.

values.title: He touched them
values.note: Took a hand, laid on hands, touched eyes, ears, tongue or a coffin.

values.title: They touched him
values.note: Power went out from him when they touched him.

values.title: His word alone
values.note: Spoken, with no touch in any account.

values.title: From a distance
values.note: The one healed was somewhere else.

values.title: Saliva, mud or water
values.note: Spit, clay, or washing in a pool.

values.title: An instruction to obey
values.note: It happened as they did what he said: stretch out, go, fill, let down the nets.

values.title: Not described
values.note: The text says he healed them but not how.

facets.title: Whose faith is named
facets.note: Only where the text itself speaks of faith or belief.

values.title: Their own faith
values.note: Your faith has healed you.

values.title: The faith of those who came for them
values.note: Parents, masters and friends who believed on someone else's behalf.

values.title: The disciples' faith, or lack of it
values.note: Where Jesus used the miracle to teach his disciples about faith.

facets.title: What moved him
facets.note: Where the text names what Jesus felt.

values.title: Compassion
values.note: Moved with compassion; his heart went out to them.

values.title: Sorrow, anger or a deep sigh
values.note: Anger and sorrow at hard hearts, a deep sigh, tears.

views.title: By kind
views.note: Every miracle once, under what happened. The fullest account comes first; the other Gospels are linked.

groups.title: Healings
groups.note: Seventeen healings of one person or a few, told in detail.

refs.label: The official's son
refs.note: Healed at Capernaum at the very hour Jesus spoke in Cana

links.label: Psalm 107:19–20
links.topic: He sent out His word and healed them

refs.label: Peter's mother-in-law
refs.note: Mark: he took her hand and raised her up. Luke: he stood over her and rebuked the fever

refs.label: A man with leprosy
refs.note: He touched the man while he was still unclean: "I am willing. Be clean!"

refs.label: The paralyzed man let down through the roof
refs.note: Jesus saw their faith, forgave the man's sins, then told him to get up and walk

refs.label: The man at the pool of Bethesda
refs.note: Jesus picked one man out of a crowd of invalids: "Do you want to get well?" The man did not know who he was

links.label: Acts 3:1–10
links.topic: Get up and walk: the man at the temple gate

refs.label: The man with the withered hand
refs.note: On the Sabbath, in front of his critics, with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart: "Stretch out your hand"

refs.label: The centurion's servant
refs.note: "Just say the word." Jesus marveled at the man's faith and healed from a distance

links.label: Psalm 107:19–20
links.topic: He sent out His word and healed them

refs.label: The woman who touched his cloak
refs.note: She touched him and was healed; he felt the power go out, then called her "Daughter"

refs.label: Two blind men who followed him
refs.note: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" Then he touched their eyes

links.label: Isaiah 35:4–6
links.topic: The eyes of the blind opened

refs.label: A deaf man who could hardly speak
refs.note: Taken aside, fingers in his ears, spit, a touch on the tongue, a look to heaven and a deep sigh: "Ephphatha!"

links.label: Isaiah 35:4–6
links.topic: The ears of the deaf unstopped

refs.label: The blind man at Bethsaida
refs.note: Led out of the village, spit on his eyes, hands laid on him twice: healed in two stages

refs.label: The man born blind
refs.note: Jesus made mud with saliva, put it on his eyes, and sent him to wash in Siloam. He came to faith afterward

refs.label: The woman bent over for eighteen years
refs.note: Disabled by a spirit, yet Jesus spoke to her, not to it ("Woman, you are set free"), and laid his hands on her

refs.label: A man with dropsy
refs.note: On the Sabbath at a Pharisee's house: Jesus took hold of him, healed him and sent him on his way

refs.label: Ten men with leprosy
refs.note: Healed on the way, as they went to show themselves to the priests. One came back

links.label: Leviticus 14:1–4
links.topic: The law for a cleansed leper

refs.label: Blind Bartimaeus
refs.note: He kept shouting until Jesus stopped: "What do you want Me to do for you?" Matthew adds that Jesus touched their eyes

refs.label: The servant's ear in Gethsemane
refs.note: Only Luke tells the healing: at his arrest Jesus touched the ear of a man who came to seize him

groups.title: Freed from spirits
groups.note: Six deliverances. With spirits Jesus spoke to the spirit; with the sick he usually spoke to the person.

refs.label: A man in the synagogue at Capernaum
refs.note: The spirit cried out while Jesus taught; he rebuked it: "Be silent! Come out of him!"

refs.label: The man among the tombs
refs.note: He ran to Jesus. Jesus ordered the spirit out, asked its name, and sent the man home to tell his family

refs.label: A man who could not speak
refs.note: Brought to Jesus; when the demon was driven out he spoke. No words of Jesus are recorded

refs.label: A man blind and mute
refs.note: Brought to Jesus and healed, so that he could both speak and see

refs.label: The Syrophoenician woman's daughter
refs.note: A Gentile mother would not take no for an answer; her daughter was freed at home

refs.label: The boy the disciples could not free
refs.note: "I do believe; help my unbelief!" Jesus rebuked the spirit, then took the boy by the hand and raised him

links.label: Acts 16:16–18
links.topic: A spirit ordered out in his name

refs.label: The widow's son at Nain
refs.note: No one asked. Jesus saw a widow burying her only son, had compassion, touched the coffin and spoke to the dead

refs.label: Jairus's daughter
refs.note: "Do not be afraid; just believe." He put the mourners out and took her hand: "Talitha koum!"

links.label: Acts 9:36–42
links.topic: Everyone sent out, then "Get up": Tabitha

refs.label: Lazarus
refs.note: Sent for by the sisters, Jesus waited, wept, thanked the Father aloud, and called Lazarus by name

groups.title: Nature and provision
groups.note: Wine, bread, fish, wind and waves. Here the instruction to obey is the usual pattern.

refs.label: Water into wine at Cana
refs.note: His mother told him the wine was gone; the servants filled the jars and drew from them

refs.label: The first great catch of fish
refs.note: "Because You say so, I will let down the nets"

refs.label: Calming the storm
refs.note: He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Silence! Be still!" Then: "Do you still have no faith?"

links.label: Psalm 107:28–30
links.topic: He stilled the storm to a whisper

refs.label: Feeding the five thousand
refs.note: Moved with compassion, he had them sit in groups, looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves. In John, Jesus raises the question of bread himself

refs.label: Walking on the water
refs.note: He came to them on the sea and called Peter to come. "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"

links.label: Job 9:8
links.topic: He treads on the waves of the sea

refs.label: Feeding the four thousand
refs.note: "I have compassion for this crowd." He gave thanks, broke the bread and fed them

refs.label: The coin in the fish's mouth
refs.note: "Go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch"

refs.label: The fig tree
refs.note: Jesus spoke to the tree, then taught: whoever tells this mountain to be thrown into the sea and does not doubt

refs.label: The catch after the resurrection
refs.note: "Cast the net on the right side of the boat"

groups.title: Crowds healed
groups.note: Summaries of many healed at once. They are not tagged, so the counts cover single events only.

refs.label: Sundown at Capernaum
refs.note: The whole town at the door. Luke: he laid his hands on each one. Matthew: he drove out the spirits with a word

refs.label: Power went out from him
refs.note: The entire crowd was trying to touch him, because power was coming from him and healing them all

refs.label: Little done at Nazareth
refs.note: He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay his hands on a few of the sick and heal them; he marveled at their unbelief
